Following Apple's major real estate expansion in the South Bay area in 2025, the company is once again extending its footprint in San Jose. Here are the details.

Apple continues to expand its footprint

According to the Mercury News (republished via AppleInsider), Apple has agreed to lease an office building spanning 125,800 square feet at 580 North Mary Avenue in San Jose.

This marks Apple's first major reported real estate move in the area for 2026. Back in 2025, the company spent over US$1 billion on an aggressive expansion across the South Bay.

That included the US$166.9 million purchase of the Cupertino Gateway complex — consisting of three buildings — the US$350 million acquisition of the Mathilda Commons campus in San Jose, which comprises two buildings, and the US$365 million purchase of the neighbouring Mathilda Campus, made up of four buildings.

Apple subsequently spent another US$216 million on two buildings on Stevens Creek Boulevard in Cupertino, bringing its 2025 Bay Area expansion to over 1.5 million square feet of office and laboratory space.

Turning back to Apple's new lease, the Mercury News noted that the deal comes as office leasing activity in the South Bay rebounds, with vacancy rates improving both quarter-over-quarter and year-over-year:

According to a Colliers report, the South Bay office vacancy rate stood at 14.1% in the second quarter of 2026. Colliers defines that market as encompassing Santa Clara County and Fremont. This is an improvement over the 14.8% vacancy rate in the fourth quarter (October–December 2025) and the 16.2% vacancy rate in the second quarter of 2025.

Beyond Apple, the report also mentioned that Amazon has agreed to lease 316,600 square feet of office space at 1000 Enterprise Way in San Jose.
